utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Theunens. Mr. Theunens, again, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Kehoe will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I invite you to focus your answers very much to the questions that are put to you. If further details are needed or further explanations are needed, then Mr. Kehoe will ask for it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in an effort to expedite this particular area, I consulted with Mr. Waespi after the break, and we went through a series of these intelligence reports that are cited by Mr. Theunens in his report. I have provided the 65 ter numbers to the registrar, and we would like to offer those. We're just going to talk about a couple of, questions about a couple of them, but the balance of them we would like to introduce into evidence, and I don't believe the Prosecution has any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber appreciates the initiative and the result. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'd clarify one point, Judge. The one document that is not, I believe, in Mr. Theunens' report is the one I did discuss yesterday that was introduced already. So in fairness to the witness I just wanted to let him know what was in his report and what was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, should I -- if I ask a couple of questions should I just continue with the 65 ter numbers, or would it be more efficient if we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, how efficient depends on your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm talking about referencing the documents. I don't intend to go through all of these documents, but I will ask a couple of questions, I think on two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently you have made a significant effort to seem to -- to streamline and to make your cross-examination efficient. So I leave it for the time being in your hands to do it as you think in this approach what would be most suitable. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could just briefly touch on a few of these documents that we've introduced, Mr. Theunens, and if I could look at 65 ter 2924. Mr. Theunens, this is a report dated 18 July 1995 from the intelligence department. And if we could turn our attention to the second page of this document. In the document it is talks about various positions, intelligence positions, but at the bottom of the second page going over to the next page, if you could help us out. It says: "After the successful liberation of the occupied area in Western Slavonia, using infantry the rebel Serbs on the northern Dalmatian front reinforced their defence line, occupied all of the abandoned positions in the zone of disengagement, i.e., after the signing of the Zagreb agreement, they intensified activities to pull out most of the brigade artillery." And there is an explanation of brigade artillery. If we could go to the next page, please, in the English. I believe it's -- I'm not exactly sure where it is in the B/C/S, but it is the second page -- the next page at the top. And it talks about relocating artillery and then further down relocating armoured units. Can you help the Chamber out a little bit, Mr. Theunens. What is happening when the intelligence report's saying they're pulling out of the brigade artillery in Oganj, self-propelled rocket launchers ... army use. What's going on there, sir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Vance Plan, among other things, prescribed that the zone had to be demilitarised and the armed forces be demobilized, which meant that the military equipment of the local Serb forces had to be put in warehouses which were under a dual-lock system with UNPROFOR. Of course there were many violations. The Zagreb agreement of March 1994 was an attempt in order to reactivate that component of the Vance Plan, whereby separation zones of one, ten, and 20 kilometre were agreed upon. The one should be two, I apologise. So that the first zone two kilometre for infantry, ten for tanks, and 20 kilometres for artillery, meaning that the HV and then the SVK had to keep these weapons out of a zone defined by these distances on both sides of the separation line or the UNPA limit. And according to this intelligence report, the SVK are basically violating that agreement by redeploying artillery assets, and I understand from the previous page that they are redeploying them within the 20 kilometre separation zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could turn our attention next to 65 ter 115.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now I must say, Mr. President, on this particular document it doesn't have a date line like many of the other documents. However, it does in the class section note that it is in August of 1995, 1 of 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Theunens, it would appear this is an order that was executed on the 1st of August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. In the first line this is a reference to Ljeto, Ljeto was concluded on the 30th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Now if we can turn to the next page of this document, and if we could just -- it -- in the third paragraph there's a comment in there about the command post of the 7th Knin Corps in Knin. I'm interested in the bottom portion of that paragraph in "the discussion of the 2nd Drvar Krajina Corps is in the barracks town centre." Now the 2nd Krajina Corps is the Bosnian Serb army or the VRS, is it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At this point on August 1st, 1995, the VRS, the Bosnian Serbs, were planning joint operations with the army -- of the Serb Krajina, were they not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know that in late July they agreed on a mutual defence pack between the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There have been several political and military agreements over time. But I'm not specifically familiar with the one you refer to, but -- I apologise. If you show it to me, then I can comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's fair enough, sir. If we can stay on this particular page. If we just scroll down a little bit on that page we note that we're talking about a deployment of Howitzers by the 7th Krajina Corps and of interest -- and at the bottom of the page is a deployment of tanks by the 7th Krajina Corps, but of interest to me is the intelligence line, "of the corps fire support group from the 2nd Krajina Corps, 4, H155." Would that would be 155 Howitzers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 155 millimetre calibre Howitzers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As well, as two T 130s and an Oganj multi-barreled rocket launcher. Did that indicate to you that the 2nd Krajina Corps was supplying the ARSK with these ammunitions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all, Your Honours, it just states that according to the intelligence available to the -- I assume it's the Split Military District. According to their information or their intelligence, these weapons are deployed in that area. Now there is no indication whatsoever that is this an offensive deployment, a defensive deployment, and there is no mention made whatsoever of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. These being deployed in -- being deployed in support by the 2nd Krajina Corps in support of the ARSK.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document does not allow to draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. Let us turn our attention to 65 ter 4505. This is an intelligence report that you discussed from the 2nd of August. And this is an intelligence assessment: "Due to the consequences of the breakthrough of the VRS 2nd Krajina Corps, forces in the area of Bosansko Grahovo and Glamoc. The highest state of -- highest state leaders of the Serb Para-states on the occupied areas of the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina have intensified the mutual cooperation in order to get the specific military results that should restore the undermined morale and stop the panic among civilians. The state of war has been declared on the area of both Para-states with a goal to arm all men fit for military service and to organise the defence of the Serbhood in all institutions and organisations." Just skipping one paragraph : "The corps special forces with the primary task to carry out the decisive defence of Knin and RSK were accordingly transferred to Slunj to the area of -- excuse me? Slunj -- from Slunj to the area of Crvena Zemlja, and Strmica." I'm interested sir, when you were -- this talks about the decisive defence of Knin. When you were a military analyst with the UN, it was your conclusion as well that the ARSK intended to defend Knin should there come an attack from the HV, was it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minor correction. I worked as a military information officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, just for the sake of correctness of the terminology we use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was our -- and when I say our I mean the assessment of the military information office that the SVK because of the -- mainly because of the favourable terrain, would try to defend the wider area of Dalmatia including Knin, but I'm not aware of any special focus of our attention on Knin. We saw Knin as a symbol of the existence of a (state or Serb-declared state of the Serbs in that area) but we had no precise information on the nature of the defence of Knin, let alone a specific assessment in relation it that defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One last document in this area before we move to the next topic briefly, Mr. Theunens. I just want to show you D156 in evidence. I believe you discussed this -- what is this about, sir, this particular document, and it is 20 July 1995 and signed by General Gotovina. If can you scroll down on the English just a bit.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a report compiled by the commander Split Military District which is sent to the assistant chief of the HV Main Staff for combat sector General Stipetic, and it includes information or intelligence available to the Split Military District according to which a number of weapons of the SVK are located within the separation zone I defined earlier. Again, it is information of the Split Military District. I'm not in a position to say whether this information is accurate or not. I know that the UN also kept records of these violations. Now we see very precise information as to the type of the weapon, the number, the general location, i.e., the area as well as the X and Y grid reference, i.e., when have you a map you can plot the exact position, in particular because of the number of digits that I used, you can plot the exact position or alleged position of the weapon that map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to shift subjects. I don't know if you want to wait for the break for evidence numbers on the documents I provided to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we can get it all together so that we go through it in the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could be provided the numbers, if we could just have the numbers now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you prepare a list and we deal with them. Unless, Mr. Waespi, if there would be any objection against any document, we'd like to hear that right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Frankly, the reader of the transcript flipping back to these particular documents, so in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that's -- that is the case now and then, but I would not mind if it would accommodate you. Mr. Registrar, this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We have seven documents. I will read the 65 ter numbers followed by the exhibit numbers. 65 ter number 609 becomes Exhibit D962; 65 ter 807 becomes Exhibit D963; 65 ter 115 becomes Exhibit D964; 65 ter number 3126 becomes exhibit number D965; 65 ter number 4505 becomes exhibit number D966; 65 ter number 5777 becomes exhibit number D967; and 65 ter number 2924 becomes exhibit number D968.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, I take it then there are no objections against any of these documents which means that the Chamber now admits into evidence D962 up to and including D968. Since we're dealing with these matters, I think yesterday there were two exhibits where you were granted a 24-hour -- the 24 hours are not completely over, almost.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I don't have an objection in relation to the maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I forgot the exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next one was the audio, Mr. President, and I will say Mr. Waespi and I did discuss that, and there may have been come confusion on my part about the source of that tape that. Was the tape that was the clip from the 65 ter the list item already in evidence. So it was a tape that was given to us. So I think with that clarification, I believe Mr. Waespi's concerns were eased.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, and no. Obviously the clip you played is part of a larger clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That is 65 ter 4467, and we would like to move the larger clip into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the Defence has no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections against that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it would still be appreciated if we would have somewhere on the record what portion, that means from what minute, how many seconds to what was played in court so that we not only do know what is in evidence but what was played.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we can take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, now we've talked about the orders coming from the General Staff, General Gotovina's actions prior to Storm, we have the intelligence reports, and I'd now like to look at the actual orders involving Storm which then became Kozjak, as you know, or renamed as of the 1st of August, it would appear. And the document that I would like to discuss with you initially is 65 ter 2614, and this is an order of attack signed by General Gotovina of the 1st of August 1995. If we could just look at the cover page first.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, quick question: Did I discuss it in my report or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I will give you the reference of where you discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might one moment, I will give you the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President. I'm just trying to find it in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, it is on page 97 of part 2, footnote 364.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could just bring this up. This is General Gotovina's order of 1 August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the name up in the right-hand corner is Kozjak 1995. And I believe this is the first document in your report that refers to that name, or if it is not, could you tell us why this name changed? I mean, do you know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Kozjak is the name of a mountain in the area, a mountain in the Dinara mountains, but I have no specific knowledge of why the name of Oluja was changed into Kozjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just stay with this order, and if we can go to page 12, and I'm looking at the artillery support issue. And we talk about the tasks of the rocket groups, and it's a -- we now find on this page on the artillery groups, so if we can scroll up a little bit more. Five artillery groups, one through five. Now that was a change from the prior orders on Storm, was it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it probably is. I don't know anymore. But I assume it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This order for the first time then took in an artillery group that took into account additions coming from the HVO, did it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that these three artillery rocket groups and two artillery groups organised the artillery assets that are available at the level of the Split Military District Command, whereby the composing units also have their own artillery assets. The document we see does not specify -- I mean, yeah, I correct that, indeed there is mention made of a number of assets provided by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular rocket groups and the rocket companies were then deployed down to the particular operative groups, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we go down to where we were in the tasks, and we look at General Gotovina's line group an organisation TS and TRS-2, TS being an artillery group and TRS being artillery rocket companies: "Along the main axis of attack, focussing on providing artillery support to the main forces in their attack operations by launching a powerful assault on the enemy's first line, command post, communications centres, and artillery firing positions, and by targeting Drvar, Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac with artillery fire." That is basically the language that you quoted in your report at page 180 when you said that there were no specific -- there was no specific targeting information on those towns. I would like you to look at the next page of this -- this order on 13, at the top of this page. If we can go to the top of the page in English, there's a bit on the top of this page that we can't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies on the pagination, and I have it maybe on the bottom of the prior page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, it says "... the chiefs of the artillery in the operative groups will draw up artillery plans of use and plans of action appropriate for the groups formed, each for their own TS and TRS." Again, TS being artillery groups and TRS artillery rocket companies. So pursuant to this order, sir, General Gotovina is ordering the chiefs of the artillery in each of the operative groups to come up with artillery plans. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Gotovina expects as we have seen in the earlier orders mentioning Oluja where it was the chief of the HV Main Staff that specified the categories of objectives that were to be engaged by the artillery. Here General Gotovina expects his subordinate commanders to determine the targets they are to engage based on the categories he has defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I note that in your report, you do not mention that particular sentence, nor do you discuss that in your report, about General Gotovina asking the chiefs of artillery in the operations groups to do that. Let us -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but I have reviewed artillery orders of the subordinate commands, and I would like to draw your attention in that context to part 2 of the report, English page 110, where I give as example the OG Zadar order for attack for artillery which is 65 ter 2209, which literally copies the order included in General Gotovina's Kozjak order, by stating, "Put the following towns under artillery fire Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean, we'll get to that, sir. And I observe that, and we will continue on down for the targeting information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 65 ter 2614.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D969.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D969 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can turn your attention to 65 ter 3124, and this is the order of attack for the 2nd of August, this one given by the chief of artillery Marko Rajcic. And this is the attachment for Kozjak 5 for the artillery. Again as we move down we now have the five separate -- three groups and five separate artillery and rocket units. On the next page, if we can, we have TS and a TR locations and firing dispositions of all of those weapons. If we can go to the next page. Actually, the following page, is 7. Excuse me, on 7. Again, it's the order by Rajcic who is the chief of artillery who -- if we can go to the last page, page 4 in the English. "The artillery chiefs and operations groups shall prepare at their own levels. All necessary documents for carrying out offensive operations." What Rajcic is ordering at this point pursuant to the order coming from General Gotovina is that these artillery chiefs are to -- are to come up with targeting information on all the targets that they intend to engage. Is -- is that not your understanding from this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- what you provide is a bit of a vague description of what should be done. It is correct that the more you descend in the chain of command, the more specific orders become. That is -- that applies for all orders. However, when we're talking about targeting, and as you have pointed out during my cross-examination, you need intelligence, you need information about the location of the targets. There is no doubt that the higher you go through the chain of command, the more intelligence assets, i.e., collection organs you have available. That explains, for example, that General Gotovina receives intelligence reports from the HV Main Staff, intelligence administration. So what I'm trying to say is that the artillery commanders or assistant commanders for artillery in the OGs need much precise information from their superior commander, i.e., General Gotovina, in order to determine the targets their assets have to engage, instead of just having a one-liner saying, "Shell the towns ever Drvar, Knin, Benkovac Obrovac and Gracac," as we can see again on the previous page of 65 ter 3124. It is not only a matter of location of the targets but also of prioritizing, because in general there would be too many targets. So there has to be a plan in order to determine which targets to engage when, not only because with the priority but also because of the location, because at the meantime you expect your ground forces, infantry armour progress, and it cannot happen that you are going to engage a target which is located in an area you have already taken control of. So in one line, the OG -- the assistant commanders for artillery of the OGs need much more specific information for the targeting of -- or the engagement of targets in these towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we talked before about intelligence and the fact that the Split Military District was gathering intelligence on troop deployments, artillery deployments, armour, communications facilities, headquarters, and I think that you refer in your report that, and correct me if I'm wrong, that this intelligence gathering was an ongoing process?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is it not reasonable to assume as a person in your position that that intelligence information is being passed down to the artillery units so they can make target selections?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the manner to transfer that information will actually be the artillery attachment or the order for artillery that is included in the attack order Kozjak-95. So I hope you understand that a town as such is not a military target, and for a military person it is not sufficient in order to carry out the planning. I mean, in this case of artillery fire, when you say shell the towns of Drvar, Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, there may have been or probably military targets in those locations, but these targets have from the offensive force point of view a different importance. Some targets are more important than others, and of course will have an impact on the nature of the artillery plan, because as I said, and I apologise for repeating it, an artillery plan doesn't only include the locations and -- in a very precise manner of the targets but also prioritizes them because you always get too much targets, and you don't have enough assets or ammunition to engage all these different targets. And that is again part of the command and control process, where by the commander in the planning process, assesses the importance based on the mission he has received from the his superior, assesses the importance of the targets and -- and other important aspects that are located in his zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We will get to these additional plans in one moment, Mr. Theunens. Just briefly, before we move off this document, which, Mr. President, I would like to offer into evidence, 65 ter 3124, if I haven't done so already.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D970, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D970 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And we need not go back to the document, but in page 2 of this document we have the firing dispositions of these particular units, and I would like to bring up 1D63-0082, which --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will tell the Chamber and my learned friend, is the information that was taken from the prior order. These firing dispositions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, we have contain the liberty of using this information and putting it on this map, and I -- laying out the 3 TRS units and the two TS units, the TS-3 being deployed towards Drvar, and TS-2 in -- TRS-2 and TRS-1 being deployed in the Tomislav district, again towards Bosnia. Well, TS-3 and TS-4 are focussed towards Knin and other locales. Now when you were reviewing this information, Mr. Theunens, and I know you didn't have this particular map, but the information. It was clear to you that part of this artillery plan was the shelling of Knin, but it was also a shelling plan directed towards the VRS or the army of the Bosnian Serbs. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably is. I haven't -- I mean, this is the first time I see this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it can help, but what I just tried to explain in my previous answer I could also explain it here, in order to demonstrate that actually you need precise planning also in relation to prioritizing of targeting and determining who is to engage what. Because when you look at TS-4, south-west of Knin, and TS-3, which is located in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you actually see that they overlap. I mean Knin can be reached, if I understand the map well, by the artillery assets of both artillery groups. Now at least in the military's -- in the military you don't -- if such an overlap exists, you want to determine in very precise term who will do that at what time against which precise target because otherwise you get chaos. As I mentioned earlier artillery fire has to be observed. The observer has to know, Well, what do I have to observe? And that's why an artillery plan will cover several pages and will be very specific, and this is the importance of that is, in my view, visualized by this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just taking what you last said with regard to observations, and I think you noted for us when you were discussing your CV that you actually went to forward observers school at one point. Did not the information that you were in possession of through the OTP indicate that the HV did, in fact, have forward observers watching the artillery and correcting fire?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. But maybe I'm not sufficiently precise. Suppose that there is military target in the centre of Knin. There will be a military observer who will know, I have to engage these and these targets. This observer has to know from whether -- from which units the fire comes, because otherwise he doesn't know whom he has to speak to about the correction of the fire. And if we see -- again I'm taking this map as it appears in front of me, if actually two artillery groups, TS-4 and TS-3, can engage Knin, well, maybe they have both observers there, but at least the observer has to know whether it is TS-3 or TS-4 which has engaged this specific target at this specific time, where he is expected to send information in relation to the effectiveness of the fire. He cannot send it to both. You mean he could, but that is not how militaries work. He has to know from where the fire comes. Again, explaining why there is an requirement for detailed planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in your 700-page report, do you reflect any information that TS-1 was not in communication with TS-3 or that the forward observers were not in communication with these individual artillery groups? Did you have any information of that you that put forth in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't because that was not part of my report. I didn't analyse that map for my report. Here I am asked to comment on a map, and I take the map as it is shown to me. I assume that I understand what the map shows, and that's what I'm providing testimony on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you did have D970 which is the attack order that we just talked about by Marko Rajcic which sets up the combat disposition of these five artillery and rocket groups. And based on that, and the other information that you had, you didn't have -- did you not come across any data to reflect that these two groups that were focussed or trained on Knin were not in communication with one another. Is that correct? Put aside the map, just on the documents that you have. And I'd like you, if you can, point to that in the report in some fashion, if it's there.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct I did not come across information in relation to the degree of communication between the artillery groups, but again, the answer I give now is based on my military expertise, and in particular the training i had in the organizing of artillery fire at the brigade level during my staff course in Belgium.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 1D63-0082 which is the map on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D971.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D971 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might just have one moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'd like to direct your attention to a 3 August 1995 order of attack from the Sibenik Operative Group. Now I will tell you, Mr. Theunens, in fairness, this is a document in B/C/S that we received from the Office of the Prosecutor that was not translated and that we had translated. So I don't believe it is reflected in your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Kehoe, you indicated on this map the maximum fire ranges for T 130s. Of course, they're all the same. What is the maximum firing rage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour. I will find out exactly specifically what that range is with data. I don't want to mislead the Court on that, but I will find that out on the break. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to be precise the artillery groups and the artillery rocket groups had also other weapons. You mentioned the Oganj or the other multi-barrel rocket launchers, there were also Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mentioned the Oganj and the Orkan rockets, those were SVK pieces.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But on page, English page 109 of part 2 of my report, I -- for example, when we look at the support provided to OG North, it includes at least, okay, four 203 millimetre Howitzers, and again I can check the ranges, but I don't know them by heart. Three 155 millimetre Howitzers, four 152 millimetre Howitzers, ten 130 millimetre guns, and four 122 millimetre multiple rocket launchers. And that information is included in 65 ter 3124. So maybe you have another map that shows the rages for other weapons, but this is only a snippet of information which does not reflect the overall situation. It is one component of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can find the ranges on all those particular weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that we can find that. But then, of course, for us to understand the meaning of this map, if -- well, if I would say bluntly half the weaponry is presented here the other half not, I mean, what's -- how -- should we ignore the other weaponry, or is there any specific reason why you included in this map the T 130s and not the others?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What we attempted to do in this map only, Mr. President, and my apologies if I didn't clearly delineate this, was take 65 ter 3124, which is D970. And the list of combat dispositions, in other words, the locations where they were supposed to be and where they were supposed -- the direction that they were supposed to fire and where the post was that they were supposed to operate from, and on this particular map, it's reflecting of these five different TS and TRS groups only two trained on Knin, and three are trained on the 2nd Krajina Corps. There weren't attended at this point to not take into account that there was weaponry as Mr. Theunens accurately pointed out, but just to clarify exactly what these dispositions of weaponry meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But what is then the use of giving us the maximum firing range, if there were other weapons with larger or smaller fire range?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I can -- I can talk to the witness about that, and he can he explain the weaponry going down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The weaponry, Mr. Theunens, was used both on some occasions -- used for operational targets but also used tactically in support of brigades, was it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question, but I will try to give my answer as I understand it. The assistant commander for artillery, when he establishes or when he orders based on the instructions received from the operational commander, to organise the artillery, for example, here in a number of artillery groups and artillery rocket groups, he will also establish the composition of these ad hoc units, because in peacetime these artillery groups and artillery rocket groups do not exist. He will use a different criteria. I mean, first of all, the location; then the nature, i.e., the distance and again, yeah, the nature of the targets that have to be engaged, because each weapon can be used for a different target. You're not going to use a multiple rocket launcher if you want to engage a military headquarters that may be located among -- or in an urban area. You will use multiple rocket launchers for dismounted infantry or lightly reinforced positions on the first line. This is again a whole process the assistant commander for artillery carries out before he issues the orders for the establishment, location, and then the specific missions of the artillery groups and artillery rocket groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we take that one step further, you're talking -- you were just referring briefly to these artillery groups and the rocket groups, operating in support of brigades. Now, they were also operating not only in shelling, for instance, in Knin they were operating in support of brigades that were moving on, for instance, trenches that were manned by the ARSK, were they not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in part 1 of my report, I have a section on fire support, where the -- the use of artillery, i.e., the purpose of the use of artillery as a component of fire support is explained. It is obvious that fire support is used against targets that have -- as I explained have been determined by the superior commander and have been considered important by the superior commander to eliminate or destroy or achieve other goals in relation to these targets, in order to implement the mission he has received from his superior commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I come back to your answer when I asked you what was the reason to include on the map the T 130s and not the others and you said, Well, what we tried to is to reflect in the map what we find in 65 ter -- you referenced to that document. Now if I look at that document, that document does not just tell us where T 130s are supposed to fire, but, if I'm not mistaken, for example, TS-3, also firing positions of the 203 millimetre Howitzers, 155 millimetre Howitzers. All the weaponry is in that document, so when I ask you what is the reason just to only present the T 130s in the map, the explanation that you limited yourself to the combat disposition as described in this -- in this document under number 2, seems not to be an answer to my question. Why you mention half -- I don't know exactly what percentage it is, but only a part of the weaponry, especially since you gave maximum firing ranges which suggest more or less that some of the cities are just at the boundary of what you could still reach, and that is very suggestive. Your answer -- we limited ourselves to this document. It's difficult for me to understand as an answer whether the document gives them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, the reason why we limited it to the T 130s was because the T 130 had the longest range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the longest. If that is the case, if the others -- if Mr. Theunens could confirm that, that the T 130 have the longest range of all the weaponry which is mentioned in this -- in this listing of -- of the weaponry, where at what positions to have them, where we find apart from the 130 millimetre guns, we also have the -- and I'm limiting myself to TS-3 155 millimetre Howitzers, 233 millimetre Howitzers, they all have a shorter range?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By doctrine, Mr. President, Howitzers have shorter rage than guns because they have a shorter barrel, but I would like to make two comments: I think it would be useful to check the information, and also then to check the scale of the map in order to see whether the maximum firing ranges, as they are depicted there, are accurate, i.e. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked for the ranges that were used on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have the information. The T 130 has a maximum of 27.49 kilometres. The 203 has a maximum range of 16.8 kilometres. The T 155 has a maximum range of 14.95 kilometres. And the T 152 has a maximum range of 17.4 kilometres. We can provide the Chamber with the background information on that which is reflected in some UN documentation on those -- that particular weaponry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I take it you say we have checked that, and then of course I have a look at the map to see how this is -- I'm -- I miss the first one. The 130 was 27 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's by for the longest. You would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would agree, Your Honour. Just for the sake of -- to be complete, the 120 millimetre multiple rocket launcher should also be included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We would we find that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Based on my information that is also included in 65 ter 3124, or 65 ter 3119, or 65 ter 3131.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know by heart what the maximum range of such a multiple rocket launcher is? Would that be shorter any way, then we don't have to go into any further details.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume it is shorter than 27 kilometres. I will check it during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do the following: If it is longer, please report to us, if not ... So the short answer, Mr. Kehoe, could have been that the weapon mentioned is the one with the longest range, which is a quite simple and quite acceptable explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Maybe I wasn't focussing enough on the point, Mr. President. It was not only the weaponry but also the direction of fire that I was trying to demonstrate coming from this particular document, D970 because it is not self-evident exactly what direction all this weaponry is pointed in, so that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I must have missed the actual range of fire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... then this being clarified, let's proceed. Of course, I gave it some thought. May I take it that the direction of fire is defined by the terrain, for example, obstructions, positions chosen. Is that the kind of -- and perhaps I should ask Mr. Theunens because you're not supposed not to give evidence. But would that limit the range? The direction of fire, of course, it is not 360 degrees, it's limited. May I take it it depends on position and terrain. If you are on the north side of a hill, you can't easily fire in a southerly direction, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Depends on your position because artillery fires indirectly, so you don't need -- I mean, that is the important -- importance of artillery. You don't need to see your target, that's why you have a forward observer. And, for example, guns have a more straight trajectory than Howitzers, but in any event, you can easily be behind a mountain, unless of course it is a one kilometre mountain in front of you. But anyway the assistant commander for artillery will deploy his weapons in such a way that they engage the targets. And there are technical limitations, some weapons are bigger than others and cannot be put in whatever terrain. But the main factors that determine the direction are the choice of targets and the location of the weapon. What is -- the terrain in between does not have -- in this context at least -- in this context, I mean, knowing the terrain in the area is not of importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, Mr. Kehoe, the map, the directions are they taken from this same document or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They're -- taken from the combat disposition section in D970.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I'm allowed, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, and with the assistance of the witness -- excuse me, with the -- his guidance to the witness, the sources of all of that are down with the ERN numbers in the lower left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that in the bottom of the map there are some. So there we find the directions of fire as well. Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just had a question, in a sense, these radiuses that are drawn, are they determined by the fact that they cover the areas where the targets that have been identified in the artillery plan or the artillery order are located, i.e., the targets located in the area of the radius, and just for visual purposes you have covered the entire area, or is it just actually you measured the range and then you draw an ark, and that should be the area they cover because there is a significant difference between those two aspects, i.e., is the map based on range of weapons, or is the map based on information that has been used at the time of Operation Storm for targets purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, quite clearly this is just a range map based on these locations. The targeting purposes are the documents that were part of the witness's report that we will get into now a specific targets that were engaged with grid references. This was the -- a view to giving the Chamber an idea of the maximum range but also the direction as to where all these particular units were disposed, the TRS units as well as the TS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we find that information, perhaps, Mr. Theunens, you're the expert, did you right down the numbers that are at the bottom of this map, and if there is any way to verify this information as far as direction is concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've got them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just move to a document that we discussed briefly which is 1D63-0010. And this is order of attack or OG Sibenik on 3 August 1995. And again, Mr. Theunens, just to give you a reference point, this particular document was received from the Office of the Prosecutor in B/C/S but not translated. So I do not believe that this is indicated in your report, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I only had access to -- of if I remember well, the order for attack for artillery of OG Zadar as well as the OG Sinj order for attack which are referred to on English page 110, part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to reference to you this document that the OTP had not translated, but it is order of attack dated the 3rd of August, and I want to turn to page 4 of this document. And while this was not provided by the OTP -- and this is the only document what he see before you. There is an note on the bottom concerning annexes from the OG Sibenik command, and the fourth is artillery plans for offensive operations and a map. Now we do not have the actual map and the plan, that was never provided. Nevertheless, sir, from this document, it is logical to conclude that there was an artillery plan with targets that were -- was done by OG Sibenik with a map setting forth that targeting plan. Would you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 1D63-0010.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D972, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D972 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now we previously in the documents coming from the Main Staff talked about the need for an artillery plan with tabular and textual information in the artillery plan. And I would like turn your attention to 65 ter 5819. And this -- I'll just wait for this to come up. Now, this is a tabular and textual part of the plan of the artillery engagement dated 3rd August 1995 for the 2nd Guards Brigade. And this sets forth, sir, the actual tasks of the artillery and the actual gun or weapon that is going to engage as well as the particular task. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And just a minor correction, it's the 7th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I thought I said that. I apologize if I did not. I stand corrected. The 7th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander here issues orders in relation to his artillery assets which are separate from the artillery assets we discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to orders concerning 7th Guards Brigade assets, and we have this document coming as a 65 ter document, isn't it reasonable to conclude that every one of these artillery units had a similar type of tabular and textual plan for artillery engagement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be what is prescribed by doctrine, and I have included other examples of this on English page 187 of part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 65 ter 5819.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D973, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D973 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And lastly in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just -- I tried to follow the evidence as precisely as I can. The issue earlier was that a number of towns were mentioned without specific targets. Now I haven't had an opportunity to go through the whole of this document. Are specific targets in this document defined for any of those -- I think there were five villages, Drvar -- well, five of them, Gracac was one of them, I think. Are there any targets defined within these towns? That's one of the things, in this document, or is it just an example of how it was done elsewhere, so that we could expect a similar thing, similar exercise for the towns that were specifically mentioned as towns to be -- to be under artillery fire, without specific targets. I'm just trying to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's a little bit of both, Judge. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document only does not list targets, it only discusses -- this page, in general terms, which fire -- I mean, type of fire and these types of fire will have defined are to be used or -- sorry. What the tasks will be of these artillery fires at different stages of the operation. This is not a list of targets. I have included a list of targets on English page 187, part 2 of my report, where we see target number, which will also be marked in the report and -- on the map and will also be found in the report. Target coordinates, X, Y, Z. East, west, north, south, as well as Z for altitude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may stop you there. So we have apparently two issues. You tell us that this document gives instruction on how artillery should be used, what function in the different stages of the operation it should have, without specifically mentioning targets. That does not yet answer the other question, whether this covers also the towns you -- of which you earlier said that you didn't see any specific targets within those towns. Does it cover it, yes or no? I'm just trying to -- to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- digest the huge amount of information we receive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can just be of assistance. This is just for the 7th Guards Brigade. And as you can see on the first, and we can go on -- this is focussed on Knin, so wouldn't be focussed on some of the other towns. So if you look at the first entry, for instance, it is neutralizing the command post of garrison and communication centre in the area of the town of Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and those kinds of targets in the other document were specifically mentioned do this, do that, do that, and then at the end it says the towns of so-and-so -- and so have been -- so we find -- I think I understand, at least a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I'm allowed. When we look at the document, it talks about brigade TS-7. What I have attempted to explain is that the Split Military District has artillery assets at its level, its own artillery assets whereby the subordinate units also have artillery assets. This specific table or document discusses the tasks of the artillery of the 7th Guards Brigade which is independent of the artillery units we discussed earlier, the three TSs and the two TRSs which had been established at the level of the Split Military District Command, and of course, that will have -- that will have an impact on the targeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, with all due respect, if I can go back to the documents, I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But sometime the documents and documents of several pages is on our screen, and in order to follow the evidence sometimes, I just want to check whether I understand what I see at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, going on your explanation when Kozjak was set up, General Gotovina took the artillery and rocket groups and put them down on the operative group level for the five -- for the operative groups to deploy, telling them, If we need you on an operational level, we will tell you. But the actual deployment and firing plans are coming down at an operative group level, and you used it at operative group level and you also use it at a tactical level. That was the big difference in Kozjak, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't draw the same conclusion as Mr. Kehoe from the documents I reviewed. From the documents I reviewed -- and we discussed the orders of attack at the level of the Split Military District this morning, we see that artillery assets at the level of the Split Military District Commands are organised in TSs and TRSs which indeed are there to support the Operational Groups. But in addition to that, the composing elements of the Operational Groups, for example the 7th Guards Brigade, also have their own artillery assets, and that is the concept of artillery fire where you can have, without going into details, artillery fire in general support, direct support, and so on, and so on, depending on who provides the fire support and who determines the targets. Some targets will be determined by the higher commander. Here the commander of the 7 Guards Brigade can, of course, for his assets which are still with him, can determine his own targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, in D969 General Gotovina quite clearly, does he not, say that the artillery plans -- the artillery plans are supposed to be -- supposed to go down the operative group level, and that the Split Military District sent those -- those orders down to the operative groups to come up with the artillery plan for each of the individual groups. And that change was a major change in Kozjak, as of 1 August of 1995; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have answered the question, I believe, Your Honours. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you do share say the conclusion drawn by Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, moving from this 7th Guards Brigade -- let us move to the actual targeting information, that documents that you referred to -- first we will refer to 65 ter 4678.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are actually several of these that are in the witness's report. I certainly don't intend to go through all of them. I'll -- the 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just take one and see whether it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this yet a more sophisticated or a more detailed explanation of the actual targets that were to be engaged by TRS-2, and it has the firing position that we had taken from the tabular text. And in this we have specific coordinates -- excuse me. We have a target reference and with the specific coordinates. So there are numbers of targets, I mean -- and then from those numbers of targets, this document reflects that they had a specific location that they wanted to hit with the X/Y coordinates. And that is what you would expect, Mr. Theunens, from an artillery unit once they come up with the artillery plan and what they're supposed to hit, they then get the XY or coordinate information as to what they are going to hit, and then they make the decision as to who is going to try to it, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the choice and the prioritisation of these targets by OG Sibenik will be based on the instructions they have received from their superior command, and I also can't want to comment this is TRS-2 at the level of OG Sibenik. It is not the TRS-2 we saw earlier, i.e., the TRS-2 that was established by General Gotovina at a level of the Split Military District Command, because that TRS-2, I mean the latter, is to support OG North.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, apparently the witness says that the TRS that we saw earlier on the map is not the -- that this TRS-2 is not the same group because it is it at a different level. The other was at the Split Military District level, if I understood you well, and this is at the level of the Operative Group Sibenik. Let first try to establish whether there is any dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is the major dispute, and the dispute is as it says here, the TRS-2 artillery rocket group, this is a list of targets that are being set forth for the OG Sibenik, the operative group Sibenik, right? Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. Whereby TRS-2 consists of artillery assets of the units of the OG Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that is in direct response to General Gotovina's order in P969 on page 13, that the chiefs of artillery in the operative groupings will draw up artillery plans of use and plans of action appropriate for each group formed. So as of August the 1st, in the first order by General Gotovina on Kozjak, when it comes to artillery, he tells the operative groups, come up with the artillery plan. The documents that you said -- would demonstrate that there was an artillery plan and that there was a map and that each individual group as we see in 65 ter 4678, had specific targets to engage, making a decision as to who was going to shoot it and what the coordinates of that target were. And that's all in accordance with the order of General Gotovina that we saw in D969; isn't that the fact?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. But the only thing I tried to highlight is that there are artillery assets available at the level of the Split Military District Command. General Gotovina, organises them in a particular manner and also determines targets for these artillery assets. He also determines targets for the artillery assets of the OGs in a more general manner. Then the OGs which are composed of different existing units of, for example, OG North includes the 4th and the 7th Guards Brigade. These brigades in peacetime have already their own artillery assets. This artillery will then, in the case of OG Sibenik, be organised in a fashion that allows to implement the mission imposed by the superior commander, and, for example, here we see the establishment of a TRS-2 within OG Sibenik. We saw earlier the establishment of a TRS-7 within the 7th Guards Brigade. Notwithstanding the fact that the commander Split Military District has also decided that, for example, 7th Guards Brigade which is part of OG North, also enjoys the support of TRS-1, TRS-2 and TS-3, whereby these three ad hoc artillery groupings are established at the level of the Split Military District Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, sir, aren't we talking about the same thing, that Gotovina has put these artillery units out at the operative group level. They are to come up with the plans. If, in fact, General Gotovina decides he needs them on an operational level he would tell them, but absent that, the operation groups are supposed to come up with their plans targeting and methodology. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I -- the order -- I mean, the order for attack Kozjak, and I still have the 65 ter number, 3119, includes an attack order for artillery, attachment 4. And I have discussed -- there's -- excuse me. There's also title 7. Artillery support in the attack order, where, sorry to repeat myself, where he establishes -- where he organises the artillery assets which exist at his level, i.e., at Military District level, and he also issues instructions for the artillery assets at his level as well as the of the subordinate units. And in the course of the operation artillery assets existing at the level of the Split Military District will be engaged, together with artillery assets existing at the lower level depending on the operational requirements. But it is General Gotovina, based on the guidance he receives from his assistant commander for artillery who issues the orders to the artillery assets existing at the level of the Split Military District Command, i.e., superior to the composing units, for example, the 4th Guards Brigade and 7th Guards Brigade and other units of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see whether I understand your answer because I think it is important there are no misunderstandings here. Are you telling us that this specification of the targets as we find in this document on the artillery rocket group of the Operational Group Sibenik does not fill in the gap you noticed to exist in the documents which sets out the targets for the Military District artillery, which is unspecific, where it makes reference to certain towns, think I there were five. That you say this may be well precise targeting information but used at a different level and does not fill that gap you noticed for the Military District artillery, where such specific information is missing in relation to the artillery to be used against towns. Have I understood your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President. That is what I tried to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the answer is the right one, the wrong one, it doesn't matter, but at least I have understood the answer of the witness. And then I leave it now to Mr. Kehoe to put further questions to you but then after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have tried to explain that these different echelons at page 110 and 111 of the second part of the report, English pages. I apologise for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which I still have on my screen, so I can re-read it again, yes. Thank you for that. We'll have a break, and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, again in an effort to streamline the cross, the document that we have on the screen is 65 ter 4678 again a document that I noted came from Mr. Theunens's report, and we would offer that into evidence in conjunction with similar documents that I don't think we need to go through, and I talked on the break with Mr. Waespi about that, and that would be 65 ter 4679 and 65 ter 5769. I have given those numbers to Mr. Monkhouse, and we would offer all three of those into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 4678 becomes Exhibit D974, 65 ter 4679 becomes Exhibit D975, 65 ter 5769 becomes exhibit number D976.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit D974 up to and including D976 are admitted into evidence. I think small portions are missing -- yes now we have a complete transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I wanted to turn bark to an item that you addressed just prior to the break and that would be your 65 ter 3119, which I believe the Prosecution has already introduced into evidence as P1125. If we could just put that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Kehoe, is there any way you would be able to communicate also with the Prosecution, I see on that list sometimes references which are unclear as to whether it is a bridge, whether it's a hamlet, whether it is Rogovo, for example. It also doesn't indicate what weaponry could be used to target that. But I've got a road is clear to me, cross-roads is clear to me, bridge is clear to me, military positions, where just a name could be anything. And if you would -- if there's a possibility that you would agree with Mr. Waespi on such -- just names whether that -- what that stands for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can consult on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we move to this document, in addition to the targeting information, Mr. Theunens, you also note in your report -- this is part 2 of 186, that "The Split Military District artillery units compile intelligence reports describing activities and locations during the reporting period. These reports also contain information on the number of rounds that are fired against various targets, including a brief description." So from the information we have again is just another level where intelligence targeting locations of those targets with grid reference and you also note that they also keep track of the number of rounds fired; is that accurate, sir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is accurate. I was only surprised by the use of the term "intelligence" in these documents because it is actually operational information, but that doesn't change anything in my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could just go back to what is P1125 that you talked about prior to the break, and if we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Maybe a page after that, please. Should be a cover -- a front page. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is, again, the larger order for which there are attachments, 1 August 1995, and if we could go to what you referenced in there which is the artillery support section which is on page 14 in the English and 12 of the B/C/S. Now, this is what you were referring to prior to the break, Mr. Theunens, and in this, we, once again see the deployment of the artillery and rocket groups down to an operative group level. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And there's nothing in that artillery support note that -- that says that these particular rocket groups are part -- that the Split Military District has some artillery group independent of these five groups, does it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But what I tried to explain before the break was that General Gotovina orders to establish these artillery groups and artillery rocket groups to support the various units or the OGs as is explained there and in addition, the composing units of this OGs, and I can draw your attention to, as I mentioned page 110, part 2 of my report, where we see here, for example, OG North, we have two TRSs and one TS. In addition, for example, for the 4th Guards Brigade, and that can be found in 65 ter 2217, we have a TRS-4 that is established based on the artillery assets of the 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Theunens, may I just interrupt you for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If can he can turn to the next page on the B/C/S. I believe it is the following page in the B/C/S. My apologies, I didn't mean to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, this TRS-4 which is according to 65 ter 2217 established by the 4th Guards Brigade is not mentioned in the order of the Split Military District. So I conclude from that, that it consists of different artillery assets existing or being used at a different echelon. The same applies to OG Sibenik. The previous document, and I only have the 65 ter number, 4682, identifies a TRS-1 and a TRS-2, 4, and I apologise it is it OG Sinj instead of Sibenik, whereby actually the order of the Split Military District does not foresee these two artillery rocket groups for the OG Sinj. And that is the distinction I have attempted to highlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's come to the crux of this, sir, that if your premise is wrong that artillery support was at the Military District level, if that premise is incorrect, then, likewise, your premise that there were no -- there were no specific -- there wasn't specific targeting information is also incorrect.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the question: The premise that is put fort is that these artillery groups that are at the operative group level, your premise is that there were artillery groups at the Split Military District level. And your likewise premise is that these artillery units at the Split Military District level didn't have specific targeting information. Now my question is for you is that if your premise is wrong, that there were not assets at the -- artillery assets at the Split Military District level, your opinion as set forth in 180 to 181 of your report, that there were no -- there were specific targets or specific targeting information, that premise is also wrong. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe these are two distinction questions. I have answered the second -- the first question, and I maintain the conclusion I draw based on the documents that I reviewed. As to the second aspect of the question, I can only conclude on the basis of the documents I saw, or I was able to review. I have not seen a document that indicates which specific targets are to be engaged in Benkovac, Knin, Drvar, Obrovac, and Gracac, following the instruction included in title 7, Artillery Support Of The Split Military District Order For Operation Kozjak which states: "Open fire or shell the towns," I mean, the aforementioned towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, we reviewed very specific target information setting fort the lists of targets that we noted which are now D974, D975, and D976. Based on the documents you have reviewed, isn't it reasonable and logical for you to assume that every target that the HV fired upon was part of a detailed list of targets with target coordinates and target numbers that was established throughout the operative groups, operating under the command of General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Kehoe is describing the situation as it should have been. But as I mentioned in my previous answer, I have not seen any documents which specify the -- or which determine the targets that were to engage following the instruction on the shelling of towns like Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned during the course of your testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, before we continue. The document we saw before the break, there we had a reference to TRS-2 I think, where the witness said that is not the same TRS-2 as we are talking about at an earlier stage. Now with the three documents which you agreed with Mr. Waespi that they would assist us, do we there have a -- to whom were they addressed? Do we have a similar apparent disagreement between the position of the Defence and the position of the expert? That's of course the problem, if you admitted into evidence documents you have not carefully looked at, even if -- I don't know how long they are, I can have a look at them on the screen. Mr. Registrar, I don't know whether they have already been --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can explain the information. I think, in fairness to the Prosecution, I should do it outside of the presence of the witness on that score.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if we start explaining that, it should be done in the absence of the expert witness. Mr. Theunens, even without asking are -- can you remain stand by, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness, Your Honour, and it may have been difficult to sift through all of this information from him, but what happened was that the witness didn't account for the changes in the TS and the TRS numbering going from documents under Oluja to documents under Kozjak. Now, I can argue with him about that, but it is what it is, and certainly at the end of the day we will discuss it. But was TS-4, for instance, under the initial documentation in Oluja, then when Kozjak was signed on the 1st became TS-2. And going through the course of the witness's report, he doesn't account for that change in the numbering which leads to yet further confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you're saying that the expert is mistaken where he says that we had artillery or artillery rocket groups at different levels because it was rather due to a change in organisation, names, rather than that these were different --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you would -- in your system if you would start counts so many 130, et cetera, et cetera, that would be - of course apart from some losses and perhaps - what you have bought in addition to what you had already, not easy at that moment, but then it would come down to approximately the same number of weapons, and actually and that's your position that these are the same weapons.
