utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The same system, except what I wanted to comment on was that initially Storm didn't incorporate the HVO units that were deployed towards Drvar and -- and in the Tomislavgrad area. And when the -- General Gotovina put them into the ultimate attack order the numbers changed, and it just wasn't accounted for, and frankly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do see where you bought some new ones. I say that with a smile, because I wouldn't expect to you place an order on the 2nd of August and to have it delivered on the 3rd. You said other elements of weaponry were added to the potential of the Split Military District and its subordinate units and, therefore, where he is telling us that it's two different sets, that it's actually the same but a bit expanded under perhaps another name, other structures, but it's exactly those same T 130s, these same assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Assets, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, of course I asked this question because I didn't know whether in D974 up to D979, the same issue which has now been explained by Mr. Kehoe would arise, and I don't know whether the Prosecution relies on the expert report in respect of these two different levels of issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, we do. And I think, in fairness to the witness, he should be confronted with this interpretation by Mr. Kehoe. And I'm sure he can give, based on his expertise, based on the review of his documents, an explanation of how he sees this -- at least one of these three documents, for instance, the first one, 4678.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think the witness has given his opinion on this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it has been -- that -- of course, I verified with him whether I understood his answer well. I would say some reference was made to regrouping and renaming, et cetera. But perhaps we should put it in a very clear and transparent way. And then see whether we get any other answer or not. Or whether he comes up with an explanation which -- I take it the party also understand for the Chamber that it's not easy to where there seems to be a rather fundamental disagreement on what it means we're looking at, to -- to fully digest and understand that material. I think we could invite the witness to come into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, yes, please proceed. Try to put it as clearly to the witness as you can. And we don't know whether my assistance would be appreciated if I feel that it is not clear enough. But let's try to -- to get to a full understanding of the issue, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, your assistance is greatly appreciated. I will try to make it as transparent as possible, and if it is not so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, with regard to setting up these TS and TRS levels, did you understand that when Oluja changed to Kozjak that TS -- TS-4 in Oluja became TS-2 under Kozjak? Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question, but I haven't drawn that conclusion based on the documents I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, of course, the next question is: Do the documents you have reviewed exclude for that possibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please explain why such an interpretation of -- would be contrary to what you found in the documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because, looking at the documents and also taking into consideration the structure of the Split Military District, which consists of brigades, brigades consist the battalions, and so on, and so on, and my understanding of military structures, in peacetime the Split Military District will have its own artillery units, i.e., artillery units which are under the direct command of the commander of the Split Military District. The same applies to the subordinate commanders, a Guards Brigade will include artillery assets, whereby the commander of the Guards Brigade decides on the use of these artillery assets under his direct command based on the orders of the superior commander. I applied that logic to the documents I reviewed. In particular, the order for attack, which was 65 ter 3119, but I don't have the P number, where, in accordance the doctrine the commander of the Split Military District, General Gotovina, orders to establish a number of TS -- sorry, artillery groups and artillery rocket groups which are to support specific Operational Groups. Then when I look at the orders of the subordinate units, I saw that these subordinate units -- you have the OGs but then we have, of course, the composing unit, for example OG north includes the 4th Guards Brigade, 7th Guards Brigade as well as other units. That these units establish their own artillery formations. Again, based on their organic or establishment artillery formations. And it is a bit confusing because you sometimes see the same numbers appear. You may see twice a TRS-2, whereas in my conclusion, we are talking about different units because they exist at a different echelon. Sometimes it is facilitated the document shown by Mr. Kehoe which addressed the tasks of the brigade rocket group number 7 of the 7th Guards Brigade, facilitated the task. Why? Because it is not mentioned in the order by General Gotovina. So that is an additional indication in my view and based on my experience that we're talking about different units existing at different echelons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now just for argument's sake, let's just assume that the artillery was organised as you told us and TS and TRS five units we have seen them. And you said artillery was organised at the Operational Group levels, could it be that when time moved on that the same assets, which were part of the artillery TS and TRS at the Split Military District level, actually were reorganised and were moved to the -- and became part of the artillery units at the Operational Group level, so that it was rather a matter of moving the assets and putting it in a different structure? Because your answer, until now, from what I understood of it, does not exclude for that possibility. For example, if I would see in one document artillery at the Split Military District level and a specific reference to the artillery assets at the Operational Group levels, then would you say, Well, can't be the same, because we find them in one document. But the time element may play a role, that what appears at one moment under a certain name and at a certain level, that it's reorganised and that we find the same assets at other levels under other names, a couple of days later. Is that -- you see what I'm focussing on, whether that can be excluded or whether that could not be excluded on the basis of your review of the documents. Mr. Kehoe, did I put the question in such a way that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please focus on that aspect in your answer to the question, whether you could exclude on the basis of the documents that there were the same assets.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the documents I reviewed, I exclude that artillery assets existing in peacetime at different echelons were, as I would understand it, based on your question, mixed up in one unit which would then actually be under the command of the subordinate commander. I have not seen during my education or my experience that artillery which, for example, in our system exists at the corps echelon is entirely handed over to a subordinate brigade commander and so that the brigade commander can use it for the missions he decides and for an undetermined amount of time. What can happen is that the subordinate commander can receive artillery support from an existing unit, separate unit which is normally under the command of the superior commander, whereby they are -- in our doctrine, but it is not the same in the HV, but in our doctrine there are different possibility that, first of all, there is a possibility that it's the commander at the higher echelon who determines the mission of this artillery unit which stays a separate unit and which provides artillery support to the subordinate commander, i.e., a unit at corps echelon, which, for a specific duration in time, provides artillery support to a brigade, whereby the mission has been determined by the corps commander. Another option is that the corps commander decides that this artillery unit which is under corps command during a specific time can -- is made available to the brigade commander, and the brigade commander decides about the mission. Coming back to HV and my understanding or my conclusions based on the review of the documents, I maintain that the artillery that existed -- artillery assets that were in peacetime under the command of the Split Military District commander at his echelon, even though -- I mean at the same time we have artillery assets in the composing units, that these assets were not mixed up, but that as pointed out in the order for attack, the commander of the Split Military District establishes ad hoc support formation, TS, TRS, to support OGs based on his assessment of which OGs needs which support at what time and for how long and with which weapons and at the same time that we see that the composing units of the OGs organise their own establishment artillery assets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now in time, when do they do that, in relation to the issuing of the attack order? I mean, I asked you to focus on time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so I gave a theoretical answer on what the options were. One of them being, apparently the last one that you can, during a specific time, make available to a brigade commander some assets and he then decides how to use them. Now, in terms of time, is there -- could you exclude for such a thing to have happened? And then you're talking about peacetime and apparently time of war, could that have happened between -- from Oluja to Kozjak, because that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The documents I have reviewed, Your Honours, and specifically documents on the use of artillery firing during Storm, the conclusions I draw from those documents, i.e., documents starting -- of discussing situation from the 4th of August onwards, show that the artillery assets or the TSs and TRSs exist at different echelons, and they are subordinate to different commanders. Of course, the TSs and TRSs that may have been established in a brigade, probably only one, are under the command of the brigade commander. Those established at the OG level, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, there is no dispute about difference of levels. There's a dispute about time. There's a dispute about whether these artillery units, at the different levels, existed simultaneously which would then, of course, exclude that it was just a re-organisation of the assets to put them somewhere else, under another name, under another command. But did you find anywhere a document in which you find simultaneously described simultaneous operations or planning of use of these artillery units at different levels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and that is what I have described on pages 110 and 111, where I state that, in addition to the support provided by the TS and TRS at the level of the Split Military District Command, i.e., that OG North -- and then we have the information on the screen -- that subordinate units establish their own artillery formations or ad hoc artillery formations and, yeah, as I stated earlier these units exist at different echelons at the same time based on documents that I have reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is at lease a difference of one day, 2nd of August, 3rd of August. I don't know exactly -- almost. We're trying to establish with great precision and detail what may have happened and what we know and what we do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, based on my review of the documents, I don't think that is one day distinction or difference is important. Or I did not conclude that that was relevant. I would also like to -- I mean, not to draw the attention away, but, for example, on page 184, I discuss a document which is D281 where we see a similar thing being done. That is in the framework of an order issued by General Gotovina, three TSs are established based on the artillery units of the Split Military District. Again, that shows that there is a reorganisation over time, because I think the key point we have to keep in mind is that the commander at each echelon wants to keep his assets under control or wants to decide himself about the assets he has. And of course the commander of the Split Military District, he will have decided about the main effort for his attack order. And probably he will have it planned that most of the artillery that is available at his echelon will support the units that carry out the main effort. And this is independent of the artillery assets these units have, and it again explains, based on my review, at the same time different artillery units exist at different echelons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: First of all they had artillery at the operative group level, as you -- as you noted but they also, the particular brigades, had their own fire support. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's actually the main point of what I tried to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Except, let us go back to your initial premise. Was TS-2 under Storm, the same as TS-2 under Kozjak?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: About which TS-2 are we talking? The one being established by the commander of the Split Military District or another one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When we had the initial orders on Storm describing TS-2, were the units in TS-2 under Storm the same units as TS-2 under Kozjak? When you were reviewing the documentation, did you make that determination?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise, but the question is not clear to me because there can be a TS-2 at the level of the Split Military District command, i.e., established by the order, I will be more precise, a TS-2 established by the commander of the Split Military District. It can also be that subordinate commander a brigade commander, for example, establishes a TS-2 which is a different unit from his artillery assets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, of course the question is phrased, I take it, on the basis of a certain assumption which is not shared by the witness. So, therefore, could you try to split it up in such a way or make reference to documents or whatever so the witness exactly knows what it is you are talking about when you're talking about the TS-2 under Storm. I think that is not where the major problem lies, but what you exactly mean by TS-2 under Kozjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to your document at page 110 in part 2. And in that you say -- I'm talking about little Roman numeral IV in addition to the support provided to TS and TRS level at the Split Military District Command, OG North supported by TRS-1, TRS-2. Now my question for you is that TRS-2, was the TRS-2 under the first Storm order the same TRS-2 under Kozjak?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to compare both documents, but in my understanding, it is the most recent document that is it actually the most authorative, i.e., that an older order is replaced by a newer order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that an answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see under IV.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first Storm order is older or precedes the Kozjak order, and irrespective what the first storm order states in relation to TRS-2, I consider in my report the TRS-2 as it is defined in the Kozjak order which is the order for attack, as the only authoritative one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the particular units, did you look to see what units were in TS-1 under Oluja/Storm, as opposed to the TS-2 units that were under Kozjak?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the orders I reviewed only indicated that the weapons that were included in the artillery groups and the artillery rocket groups. It didn't specifically state which unit was to provide these weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we go -- if we note in the document on the screen that under Sibenik it's TS-4. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go to your particular document, you note that the artillery group Sibenik is TS-4.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the artillery group established on the orders of the Split Military District in OG Sibenik. But -- no, that concludes my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can get this particular document ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we look at D974 -- if we look at that list of targets at the top of the page, this says TRS-2, Sibenik -- oh, operative group Sibenik, excuse me. Now, that, in Kozjak, is TRS-4, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that the order for Kozjak establishes TS-4 for the OG Sibenik or in the OG Sibenik, and this talks about a different group, TRS-2 which is based on the subordinate units -- I mean the artillery assets of the subordinate units of OG Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, suffice it say, sir, in the review of the document, and maybe we can just clarify in this fashion, you did not go in and clarify the changes in unit structure under Oluja and Kozjak to, as I said before, make a determination whether or not TS-2 under Storm was comprised of the same units as TS-2 under Kozjak, did you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, did I not, because two reasons, Kozjak, is, in my view the most authoritative order because it is the latest order; and secondly, in relation to the question we have been addressing this morning, I had documents from the level of the Split Military District where I saw how General Gotovina organised the artillery at his level in support of the OGs, and I have also documents from subordinate units and, for example, we saw this mourning a document from the 7 Guards Brigade, where mention is made of a brigade TS-7 which is not mentioned whatsoever in any of the orders I have seen issued by General Gotovina, and I think most importantly in this discussion is that all these units are through the chain of command subordinated to the commander of the Split Military District, and that also implies the choice of targets, i.e., because there has to be coherence in the way orders are implemented through the chain of command and also subordination in the manner as to how they implement the orders to engage the targets, and I think that is the key issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it is or not, Mr. Theunens, the key issue for the Chamber at this moment is whether there is an possibility that what we find as described as the five artillery groups under the Oluja document, that what we find at a later stage at a different level, whether that could be the same assets which were comprised earlier in the Oluja document. Now, when you explain that it would -- the targeting would still be the responsibility of the highest command, so whether they were at a higher level or at a lower level, we have looked at a matter that is how specific is the definition of the targets. Now, if a rather general description of targets is given in the Oluja document, and if it's -- that gap has never been filled, that would be a really unfilled gap, if the artillery units existed on these different levels. If, however, well, let's say, the five artillery groups were transformed, reorganised, perhaps also replenished from outside by other assets, and if we then find specific targets, then the gap might have been filled because we're talking about the same assets for which, now, more precisely targets have been defined; whereas, if they would exist simultaneously at the different levels which might become clear from planning documents, from reporting documents, from whatever, then there's a possibility that the gap has not been filled. That is, I think, but correct me when I'm wrong, Mr. Kehoe, that seems to me to be the issue at this moment. And, therefore, apart from what you would expect, et cetera, to what extent do the documents positively point at a co-existence, a simultaneous co-existence of the military -- Split Military District level of artillery groups and the lower level Operational Group artillery units, so what are the positive indications and are there any negative indications that they could not have existed at the same time? It's one of my longer questions; I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that your questions covers three aspects. The first aspect, of course, there can be a difference notice organisation of the artillery assets at the level of the Split Military District Command between the Storm order and Kozjak because it is it the prerogative of the commander to organise his assets, be it infantry, armour, artillery, in the manner he sees fit. Secondly, there is indeed a gap in a sense that we have in the order Kozjak in the title 7 artillery report we have an entry: "Shell the towns of for Drvar, Knin Benkovac Obrovac and Gracac," which based on my background, I considered unusual because I would have expected more specific information. I have not come across more specific information. It is true I don't have all artillery records available. It would have been logical if there had been more specific information already at the level of the Split Military District Command order in order to determine well, what the subordinate units are to engage in these towns. Because the units -- I mean, the subordinate units we have seen on the map, and I try to take it short, two different artillery groups that are to engage -- to that can reach or cover Knin. These units have to know who has to do what and when. And there has to be coordination with the other forces. Returning to your question now, the simultaneous co-existence of artillery groups at the Split Military District level and the Operational Group level, in the Kozjak order the Split Military District establishes artillery groups and artillery rocket groups that will support OGs. At the same time, i.e., to address the simultaneous aspect, based on the documents I reviewed they exist, there are artillery assets within the composing units of these OGs, for example, in OG North we have the 4th Guards Brigade, whereby the commander of the 4th Guards Brigade decides himself about the organisation of his artillery, assets, and their use. And, of course, all this is coherent with the initial order, i.e., the Kozjak order, and when I say initial I mean the order at the highest level because that is how the commander controls functions. There has to be coherence through the chain of command, not only in the execution but in the planning, the order itself, and the execution of the orders. If at the level of the Split Military District Command, it stated, Well, that target X, then there will be a unit -- or a unit commander who knows, I have to attack target X, and he will instruct his forces accordingly. I'm not sure if I answered the question, but I tried to be as specific as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question for you, Mr. Kehoe. When you presented this map with the rage, et cetera, was it your intention to reflect what happened on the ground or what was planned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just the planning, Judge, not a reflection because that is the reason we were trying to demonstrate some of this targeting information, and it was just showing a redeployment under Kozjak and the ground that they potentially could cover, not the actual reality that they fired left as opposed to right. And the maximum range, of course, of the 130s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- so to know what actually what has happened, that map does not assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If the Chamber is looking at that order on disposition of artillery assets, and the Chamber says, What does this mean? Where is this? What is this particular locale? I don't know where this village is. I don't know where these coordinates are. What we tried to do with the particular assets, for instance, if the group had a 130, put them in the exact location as set forth in the artillery officer Rajcic's order as to where they were and if they had a 130 firing in that direction, how far it could possibly go. It was an attempt, Your Honour, given the changes in Kozjak to orient the Chamber based on that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Theunens, one final question on the matter. We talked about these five towns, including Knin, Benkovac. You noticed that the orders were rather general in relation to using artillery for those towns. Did you, under whatever name, whatever structure, whatever difference in colour, did you ever come across more detailed targeting lists or any targeting documents or reports on specifically those towns, irrespective of whether this was TS-1 or 2, or whether it got another name, whether the command was at a different level, did you ever come across at another level a fill-in of the gap you described when you still considered these orders to relate to the artillery at the Split Military District level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. On English page 188 of the second part of the report, and that corresponds with footnote 799. I include a report -- it's called general report on carrying out a combat task by the commander of the 134 Home Guard Regiment addressed to the commander of the Split Military District dated the 23rd of August, where Cerinje [phoen] addresses the use of artillery, and this is important because he addresses the situation in Benkovac. Okay, it is titled: Corrections by the moans of artillery support were done in good time. And then I continue the quotation: "In the first few hours we had no support from the Zadar OG, except for the shelling of the general area of Benkovac, without monitoring and the message at 0530 hours of the following contents is anything falling on Benkovac." Now, there's also -- I included some entries of the war diary of the 4th Guards Brigade where they address shelling of targets in Knin, and that is actually on page 185, English page 185, part 2 of the report, and, yeah it would be -- maybe I don't know whether it is technically possible to see it on the monitor, because if I read out it takes a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We, at least -- I have it on my monitor because we have access to the documents, but if it can be shown on the -- in the e-court as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And so the source I quote from is 65 ter 4581. There's an entry at 7.00 in the morning where it is reported that: "Our forces were hitting the barracks in Knin, and they were doing a good job." Then there's an entry at 9.20. This is it still for the 4th -- excuse me, for the 5th of -- for the 4th of August, sorry. 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, it is the 5th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It reads same order is re-issued by the commander of the 4th Guards Brigade at the 5th of August. And then these entries in the 4th Guards operative log-book do not specify which ..." It is a bit unclear whether it is the 4th or 5th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we take the start of the paragraph, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The entry on the 4th of August, 7.00, and that is apparently what you refer to in the first box.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President. So we have the 7.00 entry for the 4th of August. I'm -- I haven't specified a page number, but the diary is chronologically, so if you want to see in e-court, we could go to that page. And then the next entry is indeed for the 5th at 9.20 where there is reference to an order from the OG not to hit Knin anymore with artillery. We have ordered our units and the 7 Guards Brigade to comply. And then again on the 5th at 10.38 the brigade commander asks not to pound Knin anymore, since our troops are already there. This is the information I have been able to review and include in my report which comes the closest to answering your question, Mr. President. I haven't seen any more specific information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And lastly -- one last topic, Mr. Theunens. You noted during the course of your testimony the comment on the effectiveness of fire. And I note for you, if we can just look at P64.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can put that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, I know this is not part of your report. And this is a provisional assessment done by the UN, UNMOs on the 18th of August, and in paragraph 2 -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think we have two B/C/S documents up there. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a provisional assessment which testimony reflected the final assessment was the same, but, in general, shelling was concentrated against military objectives. Now, I understand that this was not part of your report, but in our discussions in January of this year, the Gotovina Defence provided you with a copy of this, and I take it that you read it and considered it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. I mean, it was addressed in January, and I read that document and I considered it, but I have not included in the addendum of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Even after that you didn't include it in the addendum?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it didn't fulfil the criteria that apply to the addendum, i.e., documents that became available after the filing of the report, i.e., after December 2007, or documents that provide additional background to these "new documents."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you would agree with me that an assessment such as this, where it notes that shelling was concentrated against military objectives, it would be logical for you to assume that those military objectives were pursuant to a detailed targeting scheme that was done by the HV during Operation Storm. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer the question directly because there doesn't have to be a link between the planning and the execution of fire and a choice of targets there. And this report -- okay, this report expresses the view of an UNMO team that apparently 18th of August or just before made a number of observations. I cannot link -- it would be useful for me if I would really want to analyse that to see the list of targets, and then to compare the list of targets whereby the targets are identified by grid reference. Subsequently with a document where I can see, Okay, this target, target 1 located at X, Y, Z, this grid, that is the level of the effectiveness of fire, collateral damage or undesired damage, yes or not, and in a kind of systematic manner. Yeah, that's all can I say to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One last question, but it's clear after receiving this document, you did not take any of these additional steps to account for -- on the delay of this opinion that was rendered on the 18th of August, did you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, because I think it is also important to highlight that my task was -- it was not included in my tasks to analyse the effectiveness of the fire -- the effectiveness of the use of artillery by the forces operating under the command of General Gotovina. As we discussed earlier I'm not an artillery expert, so I limited myself to the aspects I can deal with and that is with the planning and the organisation of artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, you're shifting. I ask myself, Mr. Kehoe, would you expect an expert who has presented a document without having systematically, or at least to the best of his possibilities, systematically reviewed that type of document to draw conclusions form that? That is what you suggesting in the your question. And I understood from the earlier objections against the expertise of Mr. Theunens that that would be the last thing you would expect from an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What I would is expect, Your Honour, is to take that document that was given to him in January and follow it up before he filed an addendum to see if that particular document altered any of his previously articulated positions. That's what I would have expected, and that's the reason why the Gotovina Defence team gave it to Mr. Theunens in our meetings months and months prior to his submission of his addendum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He didn't give him the whole bunch. We have many, many documents of who observed what ... [Overlapping speakers] ... was this the one presented to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we gave him this, and he told us he was never provided a copy of this and never took it into consideration. We thought it important during our discussion that he see the document. And expected that the addendum would account for in some fashion, but it did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for the explanation. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would like to start my cross-examination on something that we can agree upon. And on page 317 of your report, you have a section that -- that begins on than page, and it is titled: Notice of alleged serious crimes in the zone of responsibility of the Split Military District during and after Operation Oluja. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, sir, Your Honours. I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now can we agree that you, having reviewed the documentation of the Office of the Prosecutor, concluded that there was no evidence that you found in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor that General Gotovina had any notice of any murder having been committed by a member of the HV?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to be precise, the documents I reviewed are mainly HV documents which were indeed provided by the Office of the Prosecutor. Now, indeed, I have no specific information as to -- or indicating that General Gotovina had any notice of any murder being committed by a member of the HV, but I would like to add what we have mentioned earlier; that is, the importance of situational awareness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about notice, Mr. Theunens, that is my question, okay?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is important from the military point of view in order for the commander to carry out tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll ask the questions that I'm interested, and if we could focus your answers to answer the questions that are posed to you without the additional comment unrelated to that. Now, had you a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That raises an issue for me, Mr. Misetic. The question was, Can we agree that you, having reviewed the documentation of the Office of the Prosecutor, concluded that there was no evidence that you found in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor ... Mr. Theunens, from the previous question put to you by Mr. Kehoe, I got the impression, but please correct me when I'm wrong, that you did not analyse the whole of the documentation in the possession of the Office of the Prosecution but that you focussed specifically on a certain type of documents, would it -- first of all, is that the case? Did you review any documents on reporting of crimes to whomever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is an area that I intend do cover just so you are aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you start with, You found no evidence, then of course it's important to know --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In a section that's entitled notice, Judge, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would like to explore what your exploring with him right now, if I may. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed. It was triggered by the way you put your first question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, your section is entitled: Noticed Of Alleged Serious Crimes, and I think again we can agree in the hierarchy of crime, murder is near or at the top of the list. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I'm not into criminal science. But the section is titled: Notice Of Serious Crimes, but even without wanting to launch -- engage myself in any legal analysis, there are other serious crimes like arson, looting, and related crimes. And the section covers or includes documents I did review and these are mainly HV documents, i.e., documents from the Split Military District and its subordinate units indicating that the commanders of the subordinate units as well as the commander of Split Military District are aware or are informed and are aware of these incidents taking place in their zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Again, Mr. Theunens, I think you're aware I'm focussing on murder, so let's not divert into other areas and let me challenge you on what you have just said. Your section on notice, for example, and page 323, paragraph 5 includes an ECMM report of a meeting with General Gotovina. Correct? And it also includes MUP documentation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed I said mainly HV documents I think -- I haven't calculated the statistics, but -- at least 80 percent and that's a conservative estimate are military documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But the point is that you had access to ECMM documents, you had access to MUP documents, and let me ask you a more specific question: I think I stated the earlier on, last week, that if you had a question about something or needed more documentation, you could request that more documents be provided to you, correct, within the Office of the Prosecutor. Did you ask Dai Morris or someone else in OTP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But maybe it is a translation issue. I conducted the searches myself and when I -- I mean, it's instances I conducted Dai Morris or Andrei Shakhmetov was when they would go on a mission to state archives in Croatia, and I gave them a list of documents I was not able to find. And when I asked him to see whether they could access or obtain these documents in the archives. So I think we need to be specific here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's get into that a little bit. When you're preparing a section entitled notice of alleged crimes to the Split Military District, when you were setting out, researching this topic, you would have, amongst other things, looked for and noted evidence of notice to General Gotovina of murders taking place, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not exclusively murders. That's what I tried to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not exclusively, sir. If you found notice of a murder, that would be in your report; wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever ask anyone in OTP to say, I can't find the documents which show that General Gotovina had notice of murder, can someone help me find the document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask that because I was -- yeah the question didn't come up with me because I looked at it from the military point of view, and of course murder is -- is a very serious crime, but there are other serious crimes. And the intention I had with this section was to verify whether or not the de jure aspect, i.e., that the doctrine that the commander has to be familiar -- the situation in his zone of responsibility was also applied in relation to the aspect of serious crimes, without going into detail into the nature of these crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I guess -- you're saying you looked at it from a military point of view, and that's is the point of view I want to look at it from as well. And when we talk about what -- what measures a commander should take, you looked at -- you looked at what documents he would be receiving on a daily basis and perhaps on an even more frequent basis. You looked at the political affairs reports, the SIS reports, you looked at the Split Military District operational diary, you looked at orders, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. Keeping in mind again when I said about situational awareness, that for Military Commander it is not only an issue of receiving the information but also of informing himself. It is it not a -- how -- yeah. It is not a passive kind of thing. It is an active thing. The commander has to be active in order to familiarize himself with the situation. He doesn't wait until somebody tells him, well, see what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your position generally as an expert witness coming to testify here is General Gotovina, if he had notice, should have acted, and if he didn't have notice, should have acted. Right? Is that like a heads I win, tails you loose proposition, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion is, based again on Croatian armed forces doctrine, that the commander has to be familiar with the situation in the zone of his responsibility. That doesn't only apply to the enemy situation but also the situation of his own forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's get whack to the question I asked you. You didn't find any evidence in the political affairs reports the SIS reports, orders, or in the Split Military District operational diary of any reference to any murder having been committed by a member of the HV. True or false?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer the question directly. I would need a bit of time to check my report in order to see whether the documents I included in the notice section or the section I call notice, whether they include murders or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come upon a break, and I invite you during the break to review you report and you let me know when we come back if you found the document. Let's see if we can agree on something else, Mr. Theunens, page 387 of your report, going on to page 388. This talks about the discipline statistics. Are you there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says -- it references a report. It says: "A total of 1431 disciplinary measures were imposed in the Split Military District between July and September 1995, the three-month reporting period. This respects almost a 30 per cent increase in comparison to the figures covering the January to June time-period, a six-month reporting period of 1138 disciplinary measures." We have people who are much better at math than I am in this courtroom, Mr. Theunens, but according to my math, if you take that six-month reporting period, divide it by two, so we're talking about what the average was for that three months between January and March, and then the three months from April to June, the average is 569 disciplinary measures were taken in those two separate three-month reporting periods, and then you go to the third quarter which says that in that quarter, you had an increase, a jump to 1431 disciplinary measures, if my math is correct, that means that in the third quarter for July, August, and September, there was an increase of 151 per cent in the number of disciplinary measures taken in that quarter, as opposed to the average of the first two quarters. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to review the documents, but I do agree with you, and I apologise for this error in the report which would have been covered by the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't think it's an error. I'm just saying I broke it up myself on what the map is. I don't think you made a mistake there, because I think the Croatian army changed the reports period requirements from six months to three months, around that time.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So what I'm trying to say if you look at it statistically, there is an 151 per cent increase in the third quarter, as opposed to say the first or second quarter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the quantative point of view, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness apologised for the mistake. You said there is not mistake, but 30 per cent, apparently is the mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think he said 30 per cent increase if you take the first six months. So he took the number 1138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think what he has told us is that is not a appropriate comparison. To that extent, he made a mistake, and he apologises for that, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, I'd like to take you back to some of what you talked about on direct. As a matter of background, in preparing to testify in this case, I take it you met with Mr. Waespi beforehand and discussed what topics you would be testifying about on direct. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. There were meetings with Mr. Waespi, as well as Mr. Du-Toit, and during these meetings Mr. Waespi decided about the topics that were to be addressed during my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you also in advance know, for example, what documents you would be asked to opine about on direct examination?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few weeks before we started preparation of this testimony, I made a selection of what I considered the most important documents. I handed that over to the Mr. Du-Toit and Mr. Waespi, and then that list was used, as well as Mr. Waespi added his own documents and indeed I was familiar -- or I knew which documents were to be shown to me by the Prosecution during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could have exhibit P1119 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Theunens, if you could take a look at this exhibit. It's one covered in direct examination. Was this one of the documents that you selected as one of the most important documents. You recall this had to do with an order about reporting on disciplinary measures, and then you noted about a military police post code at the end of the document and you made specific reference about who was that code. First tell me did you select this document as one of the most important?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I selected this document as an important document because it shows the implementation of the military discipline system by the commander of the Split Military District over his units prior to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, on direct examination -- if we could go to the next page, please. You made a special point of one of these military police post codes. Could you remind me again which one you pointed out and why you pointed it out.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 2233. And it's -- you can see it in the B/C/S on the fifth on the left column and VP 2233 is the military post number of the 72nd Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now why did you think it was important to highlight the fact that the military police -- 72nd MP Battalion had received this document from General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually because I was asked by Mr. Waespi during preparation whether the list included all the units -- I mean, the address list included all the units of the Split Military District, and I said yes based on my understanding of the structure of the Split Military District which is also described in part 1 of the report, I checked these military post numbers, and one of the military post numbers that is included is that of the 72nd Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My question is why is that important, why is that relevant to you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you should ask Mr. Waespi. I didn't volunteer the answer. I think he asked me a question about that, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And again I have addressed the relation of the 72nd Military Police Battalion with the Split Military District as to the situation prior to Operation Storm in part 1 of my report, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if I could have 65 ter 3349 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're moving to a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll wrap up in hopefully three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Three minutes. Then we'll give you an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this is from Mr. Lausic a document goes to the 72nd MP Battalion amongst others dated the 16 August. It follows up on the document that you just reviewed that was tendered in through direct, and if we could scroll down in English version, please. To the next page, I'm sorry. In English. Now it says: "Pursuant to the rules, you are required to record the disciplinary measures imposed on the SP-2," and that's a form. It says: "The Republic of Croatia Ministry of Defence legal affairs administration has given approval for VP units not to submit the SP-2 forms for the period of three months to the Military District command but to the military police administration." Now I note that this document is one that you specifically referenced in your report. It's at page 179, footnote 614. My question is, is there a reason that you then didn't highlight for the Trial Chamber the fact that this document that was selected on direct to show subordination of the 72nd MP to the Split Military District Command was changed pursuant to a directive by the ministry of Defence and reported upon by Mr. Lausic? Is there a reason you didn't make that clear on direct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no reason to make it clear because in my understanding, this has no relevance for the subordination of the military police. Because actually what General Lausic points out here is that with his -- this instruction or order we -- there is a -- we do not apply the procedure as it has been established, but there is a special arrangement being made, but I mean he just talks about the submission of a form. He doesn't talk about any aspects of the command and control or subordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well,' get into that. But I'm just pointing out to you that there was a document tendered on direct showing -- request for reporting on disciplinary measures. Less than 30 days later, that was changed, and so the 72nd MP Battalion would now send its reports to Mr. Lausic and not to the Split Military District Command. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for this specific time-period. We don't know later on we return to the regular situation. But here we see, yes, a change to what is normally done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I tender this document into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Waespi. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this thank would be Exhibit D977.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D977 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Misetic, time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break, and we resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Madam Registrar, if I could please have Exhibit P880 on the screen, please, page 5 in both the Croatian and English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm going to show you the regulations on the military police, and you talked about this on direct examination. Mr. Waespi indicated in court that it was you who brought to his attention this issue about the proper translation of in the Croatian text the words "upravljane zapovjedanje." Can you tell us why it was important to bring this issue up to Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I consider this important because personally I found the wording of the translations of Article 8 and 9 not entirely clear. Especially because from my background, and previous experience here, I am aware that, especially in the military, correct definition and correct use of terminology is of paramount importance. I know the Croatian expression for command and control, as in the military use of command and control. ViZ is the acronym vodjenje i zapovjedanje. And when we look at the original of Article 8, and in English it says, "under the command and control," but in Article 8 we do not see the use of ViZ, but we see the use of upravljane zapovjedanje, whereby zapovjedanje stands for command, but upravljane does not stand for control, as it would do in command and control because then would you have had vodjenje. I remember as I explained during examination, but I will cut it short. There had been questions about that in other trials, and then I checked the JNA military lexicon where there is a definition for upravljane, and I realize that Serbian and Croatian are not the same languages, about still the definition I could find actually shows that upravljane stands for management. And management in the sense of organizing, equipping, training, aspects of -- yeah, as it is defined in the lexicon, health care, as well as other administrative tasks. And I felt it important to highlight to Mr. Waespi because I considered it important for correct understanding of what is it stated in Articles 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the last part of your sentence and would like you to expound on that. You brought it to Mr. Waespi' attention. You then brought it again to the Trial Chamber's attention. I want to know why it is that you think this issue is important enough that it needed to be brought to Mr. Waespi's attention, and more importantly to the Trial Chamber's attention? What about it is that's important in the context of this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because for a military person like myself, Articles 8 and 9 could -- I mean the translation looks at first glance slightly confusing. And as I pointed out, in each language there is a definition of a way to describe command and control. It is one concept. It is not a group of three words. It is one concept. The military meaning of command and control, and I attempted to show that in the report when defining command and control, and I apologise for repeating myself, but in the English translation it says, "under the command and control of the chief of the military police administration." I would then have expected that if it meant command and control as the military meaning of command and control, it would have been expressed differently in the B/C/S version. The --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. I need to be more specific, and I apologise. What I mean specifically is what does this distinction mean in the context of the Split Military District, Operation Storm, and who had command and control over the military police in the Split Military District during Operation Storm. What does your interpretation of Article 8 mean in that context?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that for the -- as explained in Article 9 for the exclusion of regular military police tasks, the military police of the Split Military District, so the 72nd Battalion and the 73rd Military Police Battalion which was subordinated -- resubordinated to the Split Military District, received their orders from the operational commander. That means the commander of the Split Military District or a subordinate operational commander because we see that companies of the 72nd Military Police Battalion are subordinated to OGs. It also means that, Article 9, that in relation to what I would administrative aspects -- and this is not using administrative in a negative sense, but aspects like as to how to implement these daily tasks or these regular tasks, I mean the manner, the instructions are given by the chief of the military police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Whose command and control in your view -- and I used the phrase specifically command and control. Under whose command and control was the 72nd Military Police Battalion during and after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command and control in the sense of ViZ. As I explained there is the operational chain, i.e., as I referred to in Article 9, and there is the professional chain as explained in Article 8. Some people call it dual command and control, but I don't think that is the right characterize because unity is one of the principles of command and control in most armies. So indeed the military police units including the 72nd receive instructions from the military police administration, but they deal with other aspects than what we call in the military regular or -- regular operational command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. I'd ask you to make reference to specific individuals in the Croatian hierarchy. Under whose command and control was the 72nd Military Police Battalion during and after Operation Storm? Was it the military police administration, General Gotovina, or both?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both, in applying Articles 8 and 9, whereby General Gotovina or a subordinate operational commander issued tasks pertaining to the execution of regular military police tasks, and General Lausic or Major Juric issuing instructions or tasks dealing -- not instructions, I apologise. Dealing with how they should implement these regular military police tasks. This being said, there are documents included in my report, whereby again comparing Articles 8 and 9, Lausic issues instructions which, in my view, would go beyond the level of what is specified in Article 8, and, for example I don't remember the exact document, but I can I find it, there is an instruction or an order from Lausic for the establishment of military police platoons in specific areas. For example, Knin, Benkovac and other. I would have expected General Gotovina to do so. Now the document or order from Lausic does not allow to conclude whether or not Generals Lausic or Gotovina or with the involved of Major Juric have consulted about this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you surprised by that document -- is your surprise borne of the fact that you don't believe that Article 8 gave General Lausic command and control over the 72nd Military Police Battalion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I used the word "surprise." And to answer your question, actually, I would consider the establishment of -- or the deployment of military police units in a particular location, located in the zone of responsibility of a Military District, to fall within the authority of the operational commander, i.e., to be dealt with or covered by Article 9. But that is my interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So let me try to be focussed and clear here. Was the 72nd Military Police Battalion under the command and control of General Mate Lausic, in your view?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have the feeling that the same question is being asked different times. And as you see from the doctrine, I mean what I conclude from that the documents that I reviewed is that the doctrine which establishes this, it is not a dual chain, but it establishes an operational chain in Article 9, as well as a professional line, in Article 8. My conclusion from the documents I reviewed that deal with the situation prior to, during, and after Operation Storm, is that Articles 8 and 9 are implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask for some guidance here. I mean, I think the question is relatively straightforward. If he believes that articles 8 and 9 somehow deprived General Lausic of command and control, then the answer is no to my question. If he thinks that Articles 8 and 9 gave him command and control, then the answer is yes. If it is both that General Gotovina and General Lausic had both command and control, that is another answer. But at this point I'm not sure what the position is on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think earlier the witness on one of your questions said that both. But let me just find it. Let me just find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It's page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 82, line 16. You asked: "Was it the military police administration, and I understood that to be Lausic to be there, General Gotovina, or both?" And the answer starts with both. And the witness explains --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the answer is both, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including the additional explanations I gave, because that is it actually that it is all about. I mean it applies to military police. It also applies to SIS as the doctrine states, and I have explained that in part 1 of my report when I deal with the professional line and the direct or the operational line on English page 130 of part 1. If we deal with specialized units, then there can exist a dual chain, the operational chain and the professional chain. And this applies also to the command -- command and control and the command and the management of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How does your opinion then that they both had command and control, house does that not violate the principle of unit of command. Let give you an example. General Lausic on 9 August issues an order I think if you put it in through direct examination, taking away the anti-terrorist unit of the 72nd MPs from combat operations. Do you remember that document. Order of the 9th August by General Lausic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the document because I am more familiar with -- actually with orders whereby General Gotovina removes -- and it's prior to Storm -- takes away a company of the 72nd Military Police Battalion as well as the anti-terrorist unit in order to contact combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: As we sit here today, you're unfamiliar with the fact that General Lausic issued such an order on the 9th of August?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is justified from my side to ask to see the order. I don't see that I am familiar. I would like to have my memory refreshed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to get into that with you later on, but let's ask this question: Hypothetically, General Lausic says the 72nd -- the anti-terrorist force of the 72nd MPs is to be removed from combat activities in Bosnia. He issues such an order. General Gotovina, subsequent to that order, issues his own order to Mr. Budimir that says, Ignore what Mr. Lausic says, you're staying here in Bosnia with me. Who wins?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is exactly the situation that can arise if you have people who have -- hold or were in a position to issue orders in relation to resubordination, who do not interpret the doctrine in a correct manner. Now if you say, Who wins? Such issues would be normally sorted out by consulting the common superior of the two, but I realize that the military police administration is part of the Ministry of Defence and does not fall under the chief of the Main Staff, but hypothetically the chief of the Main Staff would become involved and he would try to mediated between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that in Operation Storm, if there were conflicting orders between the Military District Commander and the chief of the military police administration, they would have to hold a mediation session to figure out whose order prevails. That's your understanding?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked a hypothetical question. I gave an answer that, in my view, applies to such a hypothetical question. If you give me now a concrete example with documents, I think then I could try to give a more concrete answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand your methodology, your rationale. You've given an opinion, and I just want do understand how you understand the system to work. So again my question is: Your position is that the way Articles 8 and 9 are structured, if it ever came to conflicting orders between the depict commander and the chief of the military police administration, someone would have to organise a mediation session to resolve the conflicting orders. That's your understanding of Articles 8 and 9?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I was asked a hypothetical question, there was no reference made to 8 in 9. In my view, Articles 8 and 9 are clear, at least the original Croatian version. Now, you can never rule out that in practice there are errors or somebody steps outside his authority and issues an order he should not have issued, and then indeed through communication, directly or if that doesn't work the intervention of a common superior, the situation would be sorted out. But you have this Articles 8 and 9 and all the others exactly to avoid these kind of conflicts. The articles are clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Here is the issue. You have now just said you can never rule out that in practice there are errors and somebody steps outside his authority, and you say, in my view, Articles 8 and 9 are clear. So my question to you is General Gotovina -- General Lausic issues an order saying the anti-terrorist unit of the 72nd is to not go into Bosnia. General Gotovina issues an order subsequently says to Mr. Budimir, ignore General Lausic's order, stay in Bosnia. Under your own formulation here, which one of the two has stepped outside of his authority under Articles 8 and 9? General Gotovina or General Lausic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is, Mr. Theunens. But --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, then my answer to the hypothetical question would that be Lausic exceeds his authority, but, of course, it would be useful to know why he issues an order whereby he knows that it actually goes beyond his authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That is what I wanted to get to. If we could turn to Exhibit D35, please. Mr. Theunens, this is probably a document that you haven't seen before unless someone gave it to you since this trial began. I don't believe it was in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor. This is an order by Minister Susak dated 6 July 1994. It is issued after the regulations for the military police were issued. And in the introduction he says -- he cites his powers under Article 22 of the Law on Defence. And he says: "With a view to removing ambiguities in a system of command and control - and if you look it the original text, it's the ViZ that you referred to, vodjenje zapovjedanje - over units of the military police and with regard to the information about the failure to respect the system in the area of responsibility of the 72nd Battalion of the military police, and in connection with ..." I can't see the -- if we could scroll to the right a little bit. In the English, please? "In connection with platoons and HV Brigades on the southern front, I hereby order ..." I'm sorry it says, "in connection with VP platoons brigades in the southern front, I hereby order all units of the military police, both VP battalions and VP platoons -- sorry. VP battalions 74th SVP military police company and VP platoons attached to brigades are subordinated to the military police administration under the command and control - again in the original, vodjenje zapovjedanje - of the chief of the military police administration as specified in Article 8 of the rules of organisation and work of the military police." Now, does that -- Mr. Susak is the -- I don't know if can I put it that this way -- the author of the regulations on the military police. You are aware that those are issued by the Ministry of Defence pursuant to his authority under the Law of Defence, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's not a law passed by parliament; it's an internal regulation, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Minister Susak also has the power to issue his own orders under the Law on Defence, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the regulations and the orders are both issued by the same person, and he says in the introduction, With a view towards clarifying ambiguities, he interprets article 8 to mean that the chief of the military police administration engages in vodjenje zapovjedanje under Article 8, which is command and control. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I have seen also in an earlier document by Minister Susak a document from December 1992 which is known as 65 ter 2406, he indeed uses command and control as ViZ, but then actually the control is defined, and actually what can be found under control is administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If that is your issue now, what he said in 1992, let's turn to the last entry here in this order.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Go to the next page, please. "All orders regulating the system of command of VP units or the manning of VP units in the manner contrary to the rules of the organisation and work of the military police of the OS of the RH and to order shall cease to be in effect." So in other words, Mr. Theunens, whatever you wrote in 1992, the only two applicable orders in 1994 and forward are the rules and that order. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I didn't try to claim that the document of 1992 still applied, but I just try to clarify that Minister Susak in the document of 1992 when defined command and control and he states what command includes and what control under the section control, actually lists tasks which falls under administration, but I agree that is not a key issue. In relation to this document, I would like to go back to the previous page and see Article 3 again. Yes. Article three confirms Article 9, and, in my view, is coherent with my testimony so far. Both on -- on both Article the 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Theunens, you just testified and made a big point in direct examination about saying Article 8 doesn't mean vodjenje zapovjedanje. You now see the minister of Defence issued an order using that exact phrase in his interpretation of Article 8. How do you see that as consistent with what you have been saying?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have not said that Article 8 did not include any -- or cover any authority for General Lausic to issue his orders to the military police. I only wanted to clarify that the terminology that was used in the original B/C/S was, in my view, not accurately translated and could therefore lead to misunderstandings for people who only looked at the English translation. I have never attempted to change the language in the original B/C/S which is in my -- in the original Croatian version which is in my view the only authoritative version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I'm more concerned about is now your apparent conclusion that what Articles 8 and 9 mean in practice is in a coalition between General Lausic and General Gotovina, General Gotovina's order would prevail. And if I can just draw your attention to 65 ter 2487, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Article 5 actually here deals with the potential collision, but I have not been able to read the second part of Article 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It talks about a collision between a battalion commander and a brigade commander within the 72nd MPs.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, I see. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 2487.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just one matter. It's just so that we have as much accuracy as possible. I have just looked at 65 ter 2406. It is not from Minister Susak; it is from General Lausic an order dated the 17th of December 1992. I don't know whether the witness meant that order or another order, and it has been incorrectly described. Perhaps there can be an explanation so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what Mr. Kay tells you, does that cause you to correct yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I believe then that Lausic -- I will check the document again after court, but it is my assumption that General Lausic refers to a decision of General Susak, but I will check the document, but I take Mr. Kay' point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the annual report on the work of the military police administration for 1995 that was issued in January of 1996. It is it prepared by the military police administration and reviews its work in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
