utterances.text: If we could go please to the last page here in English which is I believe is numbered page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please give the 65 ter number again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, I draw your attention on the screen to the area that is in bold in the original as prepared by Mr. Lausic and he says: "The control and command or command and control system at the level of the VP administration," And again it you look to left he used the phrase himself, vodjenje zapovjedanje. "At the level of the VP administration and daily operations command at the level of commanders of the HV Military Districts, et cetera, functioned perfectly and received the highest assessment mark in the Flash, Summer 1995, Storm, Maestral, and southern stretch offensive operations by the OS of the RH ..." And then he continues on. Now do you agree with me, Mr. Theunens, that Mr. Lausic himself says that command and control over the military police during Operation Storm was at the level of the VP administration and that daily operational command was at the level of the Military District?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that is what I have been saying from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if that is what you have been saying from the beginning, how is it that someone with daily operational command, his order trumps the order of someone with command and control over the force?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But -- well, the reason for my -- are we back at the hypothetical question, or what is your question about? Are you referring to a concrete example here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think you understand my question here. I'm asking you now from a military theory perspective, okay, how is it that someone who only has daily operational command, his order is superior to the order of the person who has command and control over that units? How can that be?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't understand the question. How can we conclude -- when you refer to the example of the use of the anti-terrorism unit of the 72nd Military Police Battalion and whether it would be Lausic -- General Lausic or General Gotovina who would have the last word in a conflict of authority as to the use of that unit, I understand -- understood that as a hypothetical question, and my reply was based on the fact that participating in combat operations is, according to Article 10, one of the MP tasks, even though it is it not listed as the first task, and it is Article 10 of P880.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me phrase this a different way. Do you agree with me now that both General Gotovina and General Lausic did not have command and control over the 72nd, but that command and control rested with Mate Lausic and daily operational command rested with General Gotovina. Do you have any reason to dispute what Mr. Lausic wrote in his own report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that daily -- that command and control in accordance with the professional chain rested with Lausic or his representative. And that command and control in accordance with the operational line, i.e., Article 9, whereby the first comment I made refers to Article 8, that, in relation to Article 9, so the operational chain command and control resided with General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you again are imputing command and control to General Gotovina, so first I may tender this exhibit into evidence 65 ter 2487?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D978.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D978 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if could I please have D567, please, at the bottom of page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I'm bringing up for you now is General Lausic's assessment and report on the work of the military police in Operation Storm. You looked at this on direct examination. It is from the 16th of September, 1995. And if we could look that bottom paragraph on page 2. Here's what he wrote, and if we could -- I can't read the -- if we could make a little smaller so I can read to the end in the English. "The combination of the preparation, planning, leading, and commanding by the VP administration and the daily operational commanding by the commanders of the HV ZP and the HV OS made it possible to carry out all the tasks within the competence of the military police and use VP units in assault operations." My question to you is why is General Lausic making a distinction between where he says "commanding by the VP administration" and "daily operational commanding," why, if they're the same thing, why wouldn't he just say commanding by the VP admission and commanding by the commanders of the Military District? Why the qualification of daily operational?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, General Lausic talks about preparation, planning, leading, and commanding which is one group of activities which corresponds with Article 8. And then he talks about daily operational commanding, by the commanders of the Military Districts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May I stop you there. There is an translation issue here. I want to make sure -- if you look at the original. He says in the original he uses your acronym ViZ, so command and control, whereas it was translated as "leading and commanding," it should have been translated command and control by the VP administration. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure where I have the corresponding Croatian page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You look at the paragraph above number 2. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He used that phrase vodjenje zapovjedanje. So he says not leading and commanding, but command and control by the military police administration and the daily operational commanding. Why doesn't he say there -- why is -- what does this phrase mean, daily operational commanding, if, in fact, both General Gotovina and General Lausic have command and control?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it is actually -- I mean, what is defined in Articles 8 and 9. The existence of a professional chain and an operational chain. The professional chain deals with preparation, planning, commanding and controlling. The operational chain deals with daily operational command. And as I mentioned this can be found English page 130. If you want I can read out what I quoted there from the HV regulations, but special -- or units with special missions like, for example, military police or specialized personal like SIS, there is a dual chain for commanding, controlling, and reporting, which means that -- yeah. I'm repeating myself, but the operational commander, he is responsible for the daily operational command, i.e., he tells them in very simple terms what to do. The professional chain then will determine how to do it. Now -- the how is not on a daily basis, but it is the military police administration that issues the regulations, i.e., the rules as to the use of the military police. The military police administration determines the uniform, determines the structure of the military police with the different services, will also state, for example, how traffic control has to be organised because it -- you cannot leave that up to the operational commander as he doesn't have the specialized knowledge for that. And also if each operational commander would be allowed to take care of these kind of basic himself, there would be a risk of incoherence in the use of the military police. And this is exactly covered also by this entry in the document. It is just an implementation of Articles 8 and 9 of the rules in addition to the documents you present which is in my view is a clarification of Articles 8 and 9, but doesn't change the Articles as such. Because then there would have also have been a reference in the document you showed as to, well, we hereby amend the 1994 rules on the use of the military police and replace these articles by the new articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let me give you an alternative definition of what daily operational command means, and see if you agree with that. Daily operational command meant that the zone commander could utilize the military police to the extent it was necessary to fulfil his tasks. Do you agree with that? And then with respect to the anti-terrorist unit, any combat that the military police is in gets subordinated to him for combat purposes, but that he can -- he can utilize at his discretion the MPs to the extent that it facilitates or assists him in accomplishing his tasks.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all the documents I have reviewed do not support this opinion. Secondly, again, based on my military experience, I have difficulties to understand how such a system could be put in practice because it would mean that actually the military police administration has to organize an order, I mean plan, organize an order. The military police, the use of the military police battalions and companies, in each and every Military District. I have not seen any documents from the military police administration indicating that this was the fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me challenge that, Mr. Theunens, because what I have understood from the last 40 minutes, you specifically mention yes General Lausic issued this order about moving military police units to Knin and other towns, and then you say your opinion is based on your interpretation of the documents. But there you said -- in your opinion General Lausic did not have the authority under Article 8 to issue the order. So correct me if I'm wrong. You have your opinion when you encounter a document such as the order by General Lausic, you disregard it by saying Lausic must not be acting in accordance with his authority under Article 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think this is argument now, and we saw it from his introduction. I'm going to challenge you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course an expert opinion can be challenged by putting questions to the expert witness. I mean, it is not a witness of fact. It is an expert witness. So that's a bit different, Mr. Waespi. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently this expert witness -- and that's of course the issue whether he ignores it or whether he has a certain interpretation of what is within the scope of the authority of the one and of the other. And I think it is legitimate to explore why he draws the line five centimetres to left or five centimetres to the right or in the middle, and that is what you apparently doing, Mr. Misetic. At the same time we're using other notions which may create similar problems, such as you can utilize him for -- for performing your own tasks. That of course requires a clear definition of what the own task is, would that include taking care of a malfunctioning military police within your -- I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No the only thing I wanted to say is that that question raised new questions for me, whatever the answer would have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will say -- I will put my position because I always put my position on there. General Gotovina's tasks are those that he received an order from his superior commands to execute. So to the extent -- you know, obviously there are room for interpretation about something specific in an order, but if he received an order to establish check-points and control the area, then that would fall within his use of fulfilling his task. If his order is to attack a certain point, reach a certain position, then -- but we can discuss this at length. When a future witness comes, Mr. President. But let me -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock, and I notice that we have two minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can I try to use one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me get back to what my initial point was which is, correct me if I am wrong, but when you were encountered by a document and order by Mr. Lausic, specific orders of where a military police unit would go, and I think you mentioned establishing one in Knin and establishing some in other places, your conclusion wasn't, well, this must be within his powers under Article 8, and perhaps I should reconsider my own understanding of Article 8. Your conclusion was General Lausic issued that order, even though he didn't have the authority under Article 8. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I compared that order with indeed with the doctrine as well as with all the other military police as well as Split Military District documents on the use of the military police, and which are discussed in the section on use of the military police during and after Operation Storm. And in my view, that specific order went -- or I will rephrase that. Lausic in that specific order, gave instructions with which in my view go beyond what is stipulated in Article 8. And again I don't know the background for that order, whether he consulted with General Gotovina or not, whether he had particular motives to do so, I cannot draw conclusions on those aspects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, we'll adjourn for the day. Knowing the position of your language, if I would ask you to repeat my instruction, you would immediately tell me that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony already given or still to be given, so that is valid today as well. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00. We adjourn, and we resume tomorrow, Wednesday, 26th of November, 9.00, in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
